## Part 1 — Setup & Load (15%)

Load `retail_sales.csv` into a tibble called `sales`.

```{r}
#| message: false
library(tidyverse)

sales <- read_csv("retail_sales.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
glimpse(sales)
```


Report, using inline code (not just printed in the chunk above): how many
rows and columns does the raw data have?

The raw dataset has `r nrow(sales)` rows and `r ncol(sales)` columns.

## Part 2 — Clean (20%)

**2a.** Report how many missing values exist in `units_sold` and `revenue`.

```{r}
sales |>
  summarise(
    missing_units_sold = sum(is.na(units_sold)),
    missing_revenue = sum(is.na(revenue))
  )
```

**2b.** Clean the data: remove exact duplicate rows, fill missing
`units_sold`/`revenue` with their column medians, and standardize the
`category` column into a new column with **exactly 5** distinct values
(lowercase, trimmed, with underscores/extra spaces collapsed to a single
space, and the `"cloth ing"` typo explicitly corrected to `"clothing"`).
Save the result as `sales_clean`.

```{r}
sales_clean <- sales |>
  distinct() |>
  mutate(
    units_sold = if_else(
      is.na(units_sold),
      median(units_sold, na.rm = TRUE),
      as.numeric(units_sold)
    ),
    revenue = if_else(
      is.na(revenue),
      median(revenue, na.rm = TRUE),
      as.numeric(revenue)
    ),
    category_clean = category |>
      str_to_lower() |>
      str_replace_all("_", " ") |>
      str_squish() |>
      str_replace_all("\\bcloth ing\\b", "clothing")
  )

distinct(sales_clean, category_clean)
```

Report, using inline code: how many rows remain after removing
duplicates, and how many distinct categories does `sales_clean` have?

After cleaning, the dataset has `r nrow(sales_clean)` rows and `r n_distinct(sales_clean$category_clean)` distinct categories.

## Part 3 — Analyze (25%)

**3a.** Compute total revenue per `store`, sorted highest to lowest.

```{r}
rev_by_store <- sales_clean |>
  group_by(store) |>
  summarise(total_revenue = sum(revenue, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  arrange(desc(total_revenue))

rev_by_store
```

**3b.** Compute total revenue per `category`, sorted highest to lowest.

```{r}
rev_by_category <- sales_clean |>
  group_by(category_clean) |>
  summarise(total_revenue = sum(revenue, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  arrange(desc(total_revenue))

rev_by_category
```

Report, using inline code: which store and which category had the
highest total revenue?

The highest-revenue store was `r rev_by_store$store[1]`, and the highest-revenue category was `r rev_by_category$category_clean[1]`.

## Part 4 — Visualize (20%)

**4a.** Create a bar chart of total revenue by category, with a title and
axis labels.

```{r}
ggplot(
  rev_by_category,
  aes(x = reorder(category_clean, total_revenue), y = total_revenue)
) +
  geom_col(fill = "#2C5E8A") +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(
    title = "Total Revenue by Product Category",
    x = "Category",
    y = "Total Revenue (USD)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

**4b.** Create a box plot of revenue by category. Use `#| echo: false` on
this chunk so only the chart appears in your rendered report, not the
code.

```{r}
#| echo: false
ggplot(
  sales_clean,
  aes(x = reorder(category_clean, revenue, FUN = median), y = revenue)
) +
  geom_boxplot(fill = "#4E89AE", outlier.alpha = 0.5) +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(
    title = "Distribution of Revenue by Product Category",
    x = "Category",
    y = "Revenue (USD)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```
